SHANLONYI Radio with AM/FM, Time Projector,USB Charging for Mobile Phone, Large 7" LED Display, Dual, Battery Backup Projection Alarm Clock, Black-red ¡­ I use my smart phone for an alarm clock and in that capacity it works well and is all I need. However, when I check the time in the night it requires fumbling with the phone, then being half-blinded by the screen when I turn it on long enough to check the time. I looked to this alarm clock to resolve this for me and in terms of timekeeping it’s exactly what I hoped. As a radio, though, it leaves much to be desired.

The main feature of this clock that makes it worth the cost is the tremendous display. The numbers are huge and are red which does not ruin night vision. And, being always on all I have to do it look at it and know the time without fumbling in the dark for my phone. The projection on the ceiling is also great and I like being able to flip it at the touch of a button. For me, this is all I need.

However, where it fails is in the audio department. The speaker is sub-par and when listening to music to does not do well at all and sounds bad though not awful. I have heard worse. I would rather see this sell for $10 more and have a better speaker in it.

If you choose this alarm clock, get it for the display which is great and is the main selling point. If you are looking for a good clock radio and the sound is important to you, this might not be the best choice. I don’t care about the audio so this is a minor point; others may feel differently.
text_fidelity_b: SHANLONYI Radio with AM/FM, Time Projector,USB Charging for Mobile Phone, Large 7" LED Display, Dual, Battery Backup Projection Alarm Clock, Black-red ¡­

text_fidelity_a:
Cat 8 Ethernet Cable 50 Ft White Flat 40Gbps High Speed Shielded RJ45 LAN Cable I have used and tested more Ethernet cables than I can remember and there is no question, all Ethernet cables are not created equally.

Typically any device requiring an Ethernet cable will come with one in the packaging - it will work (usually). A good comparison is those cables are much like an old car - it should get you there, whereas this cable is like a high end sports car - it will get you there lightning fast, without fail.

This Cat8 is designed to be thin, but don’t let that fool you into thinking that it lacks capacity - within the thin package contains the needed shielding and wires for super fast transfer speeds. The connector bases are reinforced at each end of the wire which really help hold all of the wires in place even if you have to bend and twist it to fit it within the plug. The connector plug itself is gold plated which is the ultimate standard in connectivity.

I used this 10’ cable to run from my router to my NAS - a primary connection where speed and a reliable relay is critical - and I’ve been nothing but impressed by this product.

You will not find a better Ethernet Cable - this is really a top of the line cable that you’ll love. This is a purchase that you’ll never regret.
text_fidelity_b: Cat 8 Ethernet Cable 50 Ft White Flat 40Gbps High Speed Shielded RJ45 LAN Cable

But the real reason why I gave it five stars is this drive is absolutely reliable. I have tried other brands only to experience premature death of the drive, data loss and other frustrations. In fact, one would get so hot in large transfers that it was uncomfortable to touch. This one does not have those flaws.

I use a pair of these. One for backing up my documents on my ThinkPad T61 running Win XP, and the other as a portable music library. For the latter use I've plugged it into my Galaxy Note 3 phone and Samsung tablet via a [[ASIN:B00C7SK2J2 Micro USB OTG Host Cable to USB 2.0 Adapter]], as well as a number of PCs and laptops of fellow musicians.

Just about every operating system, from my Android phone to a friend's Win 8 laptop immediately recognized this as a drive as soon as it was inserted in the USB port.

I did not bother measuring the transfer speed because I mostly use this for streaming music via USB. I have never experienced a freeze or lag in playing, so, again, I am very pleased with it. The final reason why I am happy is the small form factor, which is about the size of a bluetooth dongle.

Bottom line is you can save a few bucks by purchasing a competing brand, but you will get what you pay for in my opinion. I've been using this brand for literally decades and have never had to worry about failure or other issues.
text_fidelity_b: SanDisk Cruzer Fit CZ33 32GB USB 2.0 Low-Profile Flash Drive- SDCZ33-032G-B35

FiveJoy 360 Degree Rotatable Car Fan - 12V DC Electric 2 Speed Dual Head Fans, Quiet Strong Dashboard Cooling Air Circulator Fan for Sedan SUV RV Boat Auto Vehicles Golf or Home I've been using this product for about 2 weeks now and I am very happy with the purchase! It provides a strong breeze of air to keep me dry despite the extreme Arizona temperatures. My only challenge is my daily driver is a 67 Mustang and this product will not mount on the dash too tall and too wide. I don't have the long center console in my car, so the only thing I can stick it to is the carpeted floor - and I would rather not do that. For the most part it stays put with nothing holding it, but if I hang a sharp right it goes sliding. Not the company's fault-but for anyone driving a 67 mustang, this won't sit on the dash. Other than the challenge with placement, i would definitely recommend this product. It's not a cure for the 110 degree heat but I have tinted windows to dim the sun and this to keep the air moving in the car. A huge help to get me through one more summer before I get an AC installed!
Edit: forgot to mention - it is not noisy! Obviously there is a little bit of a buzz but it's not annoying and nothing that can't be drowned out by your radio. Also, I like that the two fans can be adjusted up, down and side to side. So it can sit in the middle and one fan be pointed at the driver and the other at the passenger. It can tilt up or down depending if you have it sitting up high on the dash or low on the floor like I do. Anyway - great buy! Not sure why people have any issues with it dying on them but I will update if anything like that happens.
text_fidelity_b: FiveJoy 360 Degree Rotatable Car Fan - 12V DC Electric 2 Speed Dual Head Fans, Quiet Strong Dashboard Cooling Air Circulator Fan for Sedan SUV RV Boat Auto Vehicles Golf or Home

It did require me to download more apps on my phone such as Galaxy Wearable. This watch is easy to use. There are 2 controls. The step tracking seems to be more parallel to what I used to get from my Fitbit. The other smart watches were always really low in my step count which frustrated me. It tracks heart rate and stress levels. You can track fitness routines. The messaging feature is good, but I find it a little more difficult to reply to texts than my other watches. It gives you some quick replies, but I don't like the choices as much as the other ones. Also, I find it more difficult to customize my text replies with the actual typing. Overall, I do like this more than the other ones.

Anker Roav SmartCharge F0 Bluetooth FM Transmitter for Car, Audio Adapter and Receiver, Hands-Free Calling, MP3 Car Charger with 2 USB Ports, PowerIQ, and AUX Output (No Dedicated App) I had no idea something like this existed until I saw it on one of those "Best Things I Ever Bought on Amazon" lists. I had Bluetooth in my old car, and I miss it. My husband's car doesn't have Bluetooth or, at least, it didn't. It does now, and it's so easy to set up! You simply plug this into your car's cigarette lighter, and it automatically finds the radio station that will work the best, depending on your location. You switch over to that station, and boom, connected! You'll even get a man's voice when you turn your car on telling you "waiting for connection," and then "successfully paired" once it syncs up, which doesn't take long at all.

CONS:
You have to leave the car on that radio station all the time for the Bluetooth to work, so this is better if you don't rely on scanning the radio much for car entertainment and use your phone for music more often. You also have to search for a phone number on your phone itself, so it's not ideal for calling people while driving unless you make the phone call first.

PROS:
There are two USB charger ports, so you can charge two phones at the same time (or two devices that use USBs). And here's an added bonus - the charger is turbocharged! I charged my phone from 14% to 65% in a 20-minute trip - excellent! Also, I was listening to an audio book on and off, and every time I turned the car on, the volume remained the same for the audio book - I didn't have to fiddle with it at all.

I didn't even know adding Bluetooth to your car was this easy. I thought I'd have to pay $300 for a mechanic to install it, so I put it off as something I just can't have in my husband's car. But this device makes it an almost seamless experience. The only true caveat I have with it is that I have to load up a phone number to call before I drive, but other than that, you just can't beat this little device for such a low price!
text_fidelity_b: Anker Roav SmartCharge F0 Bluetooth FM Transmitter for Car, Audio Adapter and Receiver, Hands-Free Calling, MP3 Car Charger with 2 USB Ports, PowerIQ, and AUX Output (No Dedicated App)

text_fidelity_a:
Pioneer Active in-Ear Wireless Headphones with Integrated Clip, Red SE-CL5BT(R) At the price (about $40 on Amazon), I expected more from these PIONEER ACTIVE IN-EAR WIRELESS HEADPHONES WITH INTEGRATED CLIP (Red SE-CL5BT(R)). The sound is very clear, which is obviously the most important thing. However, I find the controls (3 tiny, flat buttons) to be fumbly and difficult to use. The fact that the buttons have dual functions (e.g., one button increases the volume when pressed once, and advances music to the next track when pressed and held) is partly to blame. However, the buttons seem slow to respond, so I am constantly pressing and holding when all I want is the press once function.

The headphones paired with both my iPad Pro and my Galaxy S7 smartphone, but NOT particularly easily. To place the headphones in pairing mode, so that your Bluetooth device can see the Pioneer broadcast in the device Settings, you must press and hold the headphones’ center button until a miniscule LED light on the side of the clip blinks alternately red and blue. (Normally, the light is red when the headphones are charging, and slowly-blinking blue when the headphones are turned on and connected.)

What’s hard about that pairing, you may ask? It’s in the instructions, except that the instructions are printed in type so tiny that even the best eyes will need a magnifying glass to read them. Worse yet, the key instructions are printed in pale gray (like grayed-out PC menu selections) on soft, recycled paper that is also gray. Purchasers deserve instructions that are printed in black ink, at the very least.

The clip is nice to have. The battery life isn’t great (about 8 hours), and the battery takes about 2 hours to charge via the included USB cable. The “carrying case” for the extra ear tips (you get size S, M, and L sets) is a small resealable plastic bag. The headphones don’t have “over ear” fit (as stated at least once on the product page), but are strictly “in ear” fit (i.e., battery-powered earbuds).

I didn't try using these earphones to answer telephone calls. However, considering how many mistakes I make with the tiny buttons when playing music, I suspect that I'd be hanging up a lot when I was trying to take calls.
text_fidelity_b: Pioneer Active in-Ear Wireless Headphones with Integrated Clip, Red SE-CL5BT(R)

text_fidelity_a:
Belkin VideoLink 3 Powerline Internet Adapter We tried this internet adapter in quite a few ways in our home and came to the conclusion that it is a great lower cost alternative for large homes that want to have internet around but don't have the ability to have it around the house available for whatever reason.

This works well most of the time- performance is like that of our hardline and wi-fi connections. Download and upload times were the same and smoothness of operation was also good. The only problem we had was occasionally it would cease working for a minute.

It is hard to tell why this happened- it was erratic and not predictable. Heavy machinery in the house did not seem to affect it, nor did other fluctuations of power usage. However, that workability of the internet did get affected on a few occasions, but I am not sure why. It could have been our internet or it could have been the adapter.

All in all, it is a good less expensive alternative to running expensive wire around a large home to give access to the internet. It does take up an electrical outlet for each unit, however, which could be frustrating in some situations.

Aurum Cables Pack of 2 AUX 3.5mm Male to 3.5mm Male Stereo Audio Cable - for iPhone, iPad or Smartphones - 12 Feet I received this pack as a review sample and quickly came to the conclusion that these are excellent for noise-free applications. The most critical test was when I used this cable to connect a pair of [[ASIN:B006MA9XXM Brainwavz HM5 Studio Monitor Headphones]] to my stereo. The sound was as neutral and noise free as when I used the high grade cable that came with the phones, so the claim of double shielding hold weight. I would not hesitate to recommend these to audiophiles or sound engineers.

In addition to the listening test I thoroughly inspected the physical characteristics. That revealed attention to detail like what appears to be copper cladding or gold plating on the tip, ring and sleeve portions of the connector. The barrel housing is also well constructed and is probably stainless steel. The strain reliefs on the ends are also well done and should protect the ends from internal breakdown even if you frequently handle the cable. The cable itself will stretch to a full twelve feet, but at rest is a little over a foot and a half.

What I did not test is the claim that this will fit most phones through their case. That's because the cases that I have on hand will accommodate regular cables. There is a chamfer on the barrel that houses the connector and it looks as though it will fit some of the more finicky iPhone 5 cases, but I cannot guarantee that it will for all cases.

These are top quality cables that should last a long time if properly handled and stored. If I do experience a premature failure I'll update this review to reflect that.
text_fidelity_b: Aurum Cables Pack of 2 AUX 3.5mm Male to 3.5mm Male Stereo Audio Cable - for iPhone, iPad or Smartphones - 12 Feet

text_fidelity_a:
Soundcore Wakey Bluetooth Speaker Powered by Anker with Alarm Clock, Stereo Sound, FM Radio, White Noise, QI Wireless Charger with 7.5W Charging for iPhone and 10W for Samsung I ordered the 'Soundcore Wakey Bluetooth Speaker Powered by Anker with Alarm Clock, Stereo Sound, FM Radio, White Noise, QI Wireless Charger with 7.5W Charging for iPhone and 10W for Samsung' for review and would like to share some of my thoughts after a few weeks.

First off, this thing is actually pretty amazing. The build quality is nice and aesthetically it looks clean. The sound quality is nice but not phenomenal. However for how small it is, it does produce decent sound and for a bedside alarm clock it does quite well. The wireless charging works great for my Galaxy Note 8 (and does in fact Fast-Charge) however there have been a couple nights to where my phone was not charged the next morning. The fast charger also works with my wireless earbuds which I attached an image showing the charge light on the Wakey, and the wireless earbuds case indicating charging. However for the wireless earbud charging, it does take some precise positioning to get them to charge. I noticed in other review that others weren't happy with the bright display light with no way to adjust it any dimmer than the lowest setting, however they must have updated that with a firmware update (which was super easy to do) as I had no issues with the display being too bright at night. I use the auto adjust setting which seems to work quite well as far as I can tell. Also I love the sleep mode sounds that you can adjust several (or just one) sound volumes to create your own personalized preference. I do wish that there were more sound options but the ones they provide are acceptable. I also wish that you could download and install more alarm sounds. Bluetooth connectivity is super quick and have never once had an issue with pairing it up to my phone. Really the ONLY issue I have with the Wakey is that to get the sleep mode sounds going, you need to connect with the app, and via Bluetooth connect to the device. No big deal right? Well my concern is that you will need to keep it connected for this feature to work. This means you will be connected to the Wakey ALL night and this kind of bugs me. It's just kind of creepy that the Wakey is connected to your phone all night while you sleep. I wish there was a way to just play your favorite white noise sleep sound by pressing a button on the Wakey device without having to always connect and stay connected to the app and your phone. The other gripe is that the plug design is huge and makes it so that I have had to move my nightstand further way from the wall to use it. Other than those two gripes, and the only reason for docking one star, the Soundcore Wakey is a very good product and a really great value.
*On a side note - I just tested the Wakey while watching some Youtube videos and the latency is not so good. There is quite a bit of delay and the voices do not sync up at all so I wouldn't recommend using the Wakey for listening to videos.
text_fidelity_b: Soundcore Wakey Bluetooth Speaker Powered by Anker with Alarm Clock, Stereo Sound, FM Radio, White Noise, QI Wireless Charger with 7.5W Charging for iPhone and 10W for Samsung

text_fidelity_a:
Asus Transformer Pad Infinity TF700T-B1-GR 10.1-Inch 32GB Tablet (Amethyst Gray) I debated for a long time about getting a tablet. A couple years ago I'd have sworn that I'd never have one. I've been a laptop guy for a long time and love the PC, but it gets cumbersome some times. You can't do everything with a tablet that you can with a PC, but for most people it can fill most of your needs. Smart phones are nice but they're just to small for my eyes and big fingers. Besides, my view of cell phones is something to make calls with and talk on.

That said as I read and looked at different tablets, I realized the potential for their use. I've got issues with Apple and didn't want to go the ipad route for a number of reasons. I did some research on the new Windows tablets and I like the idea, but they've got a way to go. I think they rushed it to get it to market. I like the ideas behind Android and although a lot of the apps are designed more for smart phones, apps optimized for tablets are increasing and all the other smart phone designed apps work. The open source design makes for all sorts of obscure market apps. Plenty of developers out there. You can find some weird stuff for Android that you won't find on other platforms. Lots of pretty good free apps and plenty of cheap stuff too that is impressive.

So next I had to decide on size. For 99% of my uses, the 10 inch seemed to be the better choice and with a number of these with docking key pads available, I went that way rather than the smaller versions. So then I had to decide which one. It didn't take long to realize that ASUS was probably the leader in the field and known for very high quality products. Likewise it only took a bit longer to see that the Infinity TF700 with 64GB, was the machine to have. I also opted for the docking keypad.

The tablet is very impressive. The screen resolution is right up there with the best ipad. The NVIDIA quad core CPU is a screamer. Can't get much better. Cameras are very good. Battery life is good and amazing with the dock which also has a battery in it. With all the features together, I think this is the best Android tablet out there today and most pro revues agree.

As a new user to this scene, I'm sure others may have different ideas that got me to this choice, but I can say that I am completely satisfied. That said, as a "newbie" I suppose you might think anything would seem that way, however, I did a lot of research and hands on comparisons and I'm comfortable I bought the best.

I am 99.9% thrilled with it. If it has a flaw, it's probably the speaker which faces the wrong way in my opinion and doesn't have quite the volume and sound quality I'd like. It is fine in a quiet environment, but if there's any background noise it leaves a bit to be desired. I have found that if you hold it with your hand somewhat loosely cupped behind the speaker, the sound level improves dramatically as your hand reflects if towrd you. It is fine with ear buds and I also recently picked up a great little bluetooth speaker, (Clalrity HD by Monster), that kicks butt.

Everything else about the Infinity TF700 seems perfect. The only other way to make it better would be built in 4G and phone capability. If I'm mobile I use mine with a Verizon Jet Pack, which is an awesome device itself. Even on 3G it works better than my built in mobile broadband in my laptop.

Do your own research and get some hands on time if you can to compare because all tablets are not equal. There is no doubt that as far as tablets go, a lot has to do with how you will use it and what for. But if you want the best Android tablet in the 10 inch size range, you can't beat the Infinity TF700. This thing is awesome!
text_fidelity_b: Asus Transformer Pad Infinity TF700T-B1-GR 10.1-Inch 32GB Tablet (Amethyst Gray)

It looked perfect for my oldest son who is a huge 80's music fan and thought he should hear it in its original format. We were excited to unbox it and play the two albums we picked up at the used book store. First impressions were OK. The case looks nice and love the two speakers built in. Opening it, we were underwhelmed by the plastic turntable, stylus arm and rather cheap looking controls. But we were still excited.

The sound was also a little disappointing. The two speakers are underpowered and all high end so it was pretty tinny. But the absolute worst was that they stylus is so head light that it skipped constantly. We put a small glass bead on it and the weight actually slowed the turntable. We backed off and placed a quarter on it and it played about right. But again, I was underwhelmed by the underpowered turntable. Also, we noted that one of the spongy pads on the turn table was not installed properly and put a list to the album. We fixed that and fixed the quarter to the stylus and we were able to get it to play through Adam Ant's Friend or Foe album. The scratchy quality of between songs brought me back 40 years to my own first phonograph, which I think was pretty crappy, but probably better than this one.

It works, its nostalgic. We have had fun and will probably get an album at every used bookstore, garage sale, or antique store we find them in, but we will need to upgrade if he goes beyond just enjoying the novelty of it.

text_fidelity_a:
DEWALT DXFRS800 2 Watt Heavy Duty Walkie Talkies - Waterproof, Shock Resistant, Long Range & Rechargeable Two-Way Radio with VOX My husband has a lot of use for communication on jobs he has to do in the contracting world. We have had some jobs here at the house which required walkie talkie communication. Let's see how these performed.

WHAT ARE THESE LIKE?
HOW ARE THEY BUILT?
These walkie talkies are tough. They come with the batteries outside of the units, so you have to put them in.

HOW TO PUT BATTERIES IN
You will need a very pointed screwdriver or a small Phillips head screw driver to get the battery cover off. When you screw it back in, it is pretty sturdy.

HOW TO TURN IT ON
The on button on the top is large and easy to cold, dirty, or gloved hands to turn on and off. You can also adjust volume.

CASE?
The case snaps on and off of the units. They stay hooked to the clothes pretty well as long as you are not moving around a lot. In that case, we found them most useful to hold the walkies in the pockets with the clip.

CLARITY OF SOUND?
The clarity of sound was superb. We were doing roof work on the top of a third story and they worked great. We also had to do work about 100 ft away from the point of origin of a wiring job, so we needed that for communication to test the connections. Again, they worked great. Very clear and worked very well.

TOUGH?
These have been dropped a few times and worked very well.

RECHARGING?
The recharging unit has a place for both walkies to be charged. The plug is separate from the base that you charge in. Each receptacle has a red light on it to let you know that the walkie is charging. The plug is small so you can use it on a power strip or in the wall outlet without blocking other outlets. Recharging is fast- within the hour- and they seem to last quite a while before needing to be recharged.

CLIPS
The clips have to be removed prior to charging.

CHANNELS
The different channels we used all worked well. We did not have to use them in a very busy area with multiple walkies, however, so we did not get to test it with a lot of walkie talkie traffic happening on a huge job site.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For a very sturdy set of walkie talkies which charge up quickly and last a long time, these are fantastic for contract work and any jobs that we have had to do. My husband plans to take them to his jobs as well when needed. They have a decent range to them and are easy to operate even with gloves on.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. We really love these walkie-talkies. They have been fantastic so far for all of the jobs we have had to use them for. I will update if we have anything valuable to add in the future as we continue to use them over time.
text_fidelity_b: DEWALT DXFRS800 2 Watt Heavy Duty Walkie Talkies - Waterproof, Shock Resistant, Long Range & Rechargeable Two-Way Radio with VOX

CyberPower CSP604UMP6 Professional Surge Protector, 1200J/125V, 6 Outlets, 2 USB Charge Ports, 4ft Power Cord, 6 Pack , Black The irony here is that I bought this to replace a 20 year old surge protector whose opposite end from where the power cable enters the device was getting so hot, the beige plastic was showing burn marks. I thought with all the technological advancements, 6 AC plugs (the same as the old one) and 2 USB ports, I should fit a device or 2 extra on the new one. Nope. These plugs are so close together, even a plug that is just slightly larger than a standard grounded plug will cause an overlap on the plug next to it thereby rendering the neighboring plug unavailable. Despite going from an 6 AC plug surge protector power strip to an 6 AC plug surge protector power strip, I went from being able to fit 5 plugs in the old strip to only being able, in the best configuration possible, to fit 4 plugs.

I was lucky that I had one plug that was a Samsung wall charger with a Samsung USB charger cable. Since I had to lose something, that was the only one I could lose, but still put on the strip. So what? I was not expecting to lose 1 of the 2 USB chargers to accommodate one of the plugs that had to get bumped.

I probably would have gotten over that, but then when I went to test the performance of the USB charging ports, they fell short. With the Samsung manufactured original cable for my S5, this port only charged at 1.15A. To validate it, I took it to several other devices in the house and with the same S5 device, Samsung wall plug and original cable and the same meter, the S5 pulled 1.75A out of both the Samsung wall charger and the 5 port USB charger that I also bought from Amazon (I have a review there, too).

I gave it 2 stars because overall, this is not such a disaster that I would waste my time and money returning it. There are soooo many surge protector power chargers with USB charge ports on Amazon that at least one of them has to be better than this.

text_fidelity_a:
Magellan Triton 400 Waterproof Hiking GPS UPDATE 11-30-2009: I initially gave this unit a rating of 3 stars. I am upgrading it to 4 stars because of a firmware upgrade that vastly improved the speed of the unit and eliminated issues I saw with VantagePoint. That said, I am leaving my original write-up intact.

---

I am an avid geocacher, and I have other hand-held units by Garmin and DeLorme. I have never used a Magellan GPS though I have friends who have used an Explorist for years with reasonable results. I was anxious to try out this unit to see if Magellan puts out a good product. In a nutshell, it is a mixed bag though overall the Triton 400 is a nice unit.

This is a very small unit, a little smaller than my Garmin eTrex Legend which is a fairly simple unit. Small is not necessarily a bad thing. It fits nicely in a pocket or a stash bag, being about the size of a cell phone.

The display is small too and people who want a large display will not like this unit. That said, the display is very bright, crisp and clear, everything being quite visible and readable. It had, in my opinion, the best general display of the units I have used, surpassing even the DeLorme in display quality.

Once the unit is powered on, it quickly starts finding satellites. Though it switches to navigation mode quickly, it is important to remember that the unit may or may not have a good lock on satellites - it may still be acquiring more. Be cautious in this regard, until used to using this unit.

The Triton has small buttons. I have big fingers. Surprisingly, this does not seem to be an issue, as I have not yet had the misfortune of mis-keying anything.

Several reviewers have complained that the menu system on the Triton is confusing, unintuitive and hard to use. I did not find this to be the case. I can simply say they are different than Garmin's implementations. That is neither good nor bad - just, different. Once used to them, this unit is no less intuitive than any other unit.

Navigation is straightforward and easy. When navigating I have found the unit to be on par with my Garmin GPSMap 60CSx, which is usually fairly accurate. I've no complaints in this regard.

My disappointment with the Triton mostly involve what's [not] in the box and the software that the computer uses to interact with it. There is a single CD in the box that includes PDF versions of the manual. There are no printed manuals in the box, at all. This is ok, but other units include a manual so it would be nice if this one did too. There is also a link to the website where you can download Vantage Point, the software for working with the unit. The software is 42MB, and I am on dial-up. Even including an older version would have been nice since there is plenty of room on the CD for it...

When the software is loaded on a Windows Vista machine, system behavior becomes very sluggish, mouse movement being choppy and COM port communications getting interruptions - enough interruptions to disconnect from the Internet. Though the software has eye appeal and offers a lot of functionality for dealing with the GPS, it drips of slowness. When sending caches to the unit, it sends at a rate of about 1 every 5-10 seconds, which means sending 500 at a time would take a good deal of time. That said, geocache information stops a little shy of being a paperless solution - the unit retains description, terrain/difficulty, owner and hint information, but it does not offer previous logs, sizes or other important bits of information. It's a good reference in the field but not sufficient to go true paperless.

Though there is a place on the bottom of the unit for a lanyard, it is disappointing that there is none in the box.

One area of real concern for me is the connection interface for the unit. The connector on the unit is exposed and uncovered, with nothing to keep it from getting dirty. If nothing else there should be a rubber flap over it, or a cover, or *something*.

This is actually a nice unit, with a decent feature set and good accuracy. Magellan cut some corners and left out some details that keep this from being a great unit. The technology is there. The design is there. The details are not. Hopefully Magellan will close the gap on these details soon.
text_fidelity_b: Magellan Triton 400 Waterproof Hiking GPS

text_fidelity_a:
Fire Tablet with Alexa, 7" Display, 16 GB, Blue - with Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th) If you're looking for an excellent tablet and e-reader at a great price, look no further. While there are things that it lags with (like playing the Pokemon trading card game, which last I knew, needed to be sideloaded) it does a lot of other things really well. Great experience with watching videos, and reading comics or manga.

If you're into hacking your devices, this tablet (well, the 2015 version that I have) does a really good job of running a clean Nexus rom, which gives you a stock Android experience, and access to the Google play store. I have to say, that was probably the best thing I've done with it so far.

Expandable storage allows you to carry an entire library with you on the go to make sure that you will never run out of things to do. I keep a 128gb micro SD card in mine, but I wouldn't be surprised if you could slot in a larger card, even though it's only officially rated for up to 128gb.

What i'd like to see change for the 2018 version (assuming they do a revamp) would be full 1080p resolution, a snapdragon octacore processor clocked around 2ghz (my free ZTE Blade Zmax has one, and I can't imagine it would be too expensive for them to use it in the fire tablet as well, if even free phones have them now) and 2-3 gb of ram. If Amazon would just do these 3 little upgrades, this tablet would be unbeatable. I wouldn't even mind a mild price bump ($70-80 instead of $50) if these upgrades happened. I would also like to see a future version either running full stock Android OS, or released with the option to unlock the bootloader somehow, to facilitate diy development and cutom roms. But I know that's just asking too much.

If you're looking for a great tablet at an even better price, the Fire 7" is a great choice.
text_fidelity_b: Fire Tablet with Alexa, 7" Display, 16 GB, Blue - with Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th)

text_fidelity_a:
Sony ICF-506 Analog Tuning Portable FM/AM Radio, Black, 2.14 lb It is harder and harder to find any radio that has an AM radio band on it, let alone a really good one. It is also rather difficult to find a decent radio that is not digitally tuned and controlled. This radio is a good solid radio with both of the above features on it.

WHAT IS THIS RADIO LIKE?
This radio is a good solid radio. It has a slide switch under the tuning bar which has three settings - OFF, AM, and FM. On the right side are two dials. There is one with volume that goes from Minimum to Maximum. The other dial is the tuning dial. That makes the tuning bar slide up and down for both AM and FM. There is a handle on top that flips up or goes down. There is a pull out telescopic antenna on the top for better reception. There is a place in the left side where you plug in the electric cord, but you can remove it if you prefer to operate solely by batteries. The cord is a little over 5 feet long. The plug is a two pronged plug and is polarized. There is a door on the back which slides off and allows you to put in 3 AA batteries. The door has attached hinges so you don't have to worry about losing the battery door off of the unit unless it breaks.

HOW DOES THIS RADIO PERFORM?
For AM I would say that it has okay reception It is not WOW but it is not terrible either. Since AM is not really dominating the airwaves anymore, I imagine that some people would not find this to be a problem. If you want really strong AM reception, this is okay, but you might be able to find better.

For FM reception, the radio is great. It pulls in quite a few stations and also plays them very clearly. The speaker is best showcased by FM. It is a full sound and impressive considering the size of the speaker and the basic nature of the radio. I found that it is a nice sound and enjoyable.

HANDLE
The handle has a bit of a recoil to help it snap back into place, but it does seem just a little bit flimsy to me. I wish it was just a bit sturdier. It is not enough to take off a star.

WHAT WOULD THIS RADIO COME IN HANDY FOR?
For those of you who are from the era where radios of this nature were commonplace, I am not writing this comment section for you. You already know what this would be good for. For those of you who think that In Tune, or other internet radio stations would suffice for any AM or FM radio stations, I would like to mention that during weather crises, that AM/FM and shortwave radio tend to be the only reception you can get if any. That includes disasters. At that point, internet is not an option, so it is important to have a back up communication capability to keep up on what is going on and any emergency information that might come up, or even information about upcoming help.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This radio is handy. It is a decent size, sturdy, and a solid basic radio. It gets decent reception and has a nice speaker which is especially nice for FM. During emergencies and times of crises, this is a good backup to have should internet not be an option. Running on both electricity and AA batteries, this would be a great addition to your basic emergency kit.

MY RATING
Despite the handle being a bit flimsier than I would like, it is still decent and a solid radio. I do not think that it is worth taking off a star.
text_fidelity_b: Sony ICF-506 Analog Tuning Portable FM/AM Radio, Black, 2.14 lb

text_fidelity_a:
TP-Link AC1900 Smart Wireless Router - Beamforming Dual Band Gigabit WiFi Internet Routers for Home, High Speed, Long Range, Ideal for Gaming (Archer C9) Okay, I realize that everyone's definition of "easy to set up" comes from a different place. For me, I've worked around computers for over 25 years now, so pretty comfortable, BUT - I am more comfortable with software than hardware. So although this should not have been intimidating, it was a little bit. I formerly was using a Linksys router on our home network. It did a fine job, and was very easy to maintain. However, it didn't give much of a boost to the downstairs connections. The computer was always slow, and would drop the connection from time to time, and require a reboot to get the connection back.

This router is truly great looking. It is white, sleek and has nice blue lights. It sits vertically, rather than horizontally like my old one. I wasn't sure I'd like it, but I do. It comes with three screw-on antennas that can be pointed in any direction to boost your signal in that direction. The metal frame is very sturdy and would take a LOT of pressure to bend. I currently have mine on a separate little shelf because my current desk is too small.

There is only a quick set-up sheet included with this item. Ironically, if you need help, it tells you to go to the company's WEBSITE! Ha! So, if you can't get it to work, go ahead and get online. Yeah, No. But, if you are willing to disconnect and reset up a single-user home network using your old router, it could work! The sheet does give you very plain graphic instructions that tells you which item to plug in where, which many will find very helpful It came with a very short ethernet cord, so you either need to keep the router close to you or buy a longer cord. (The one I had was just purchased last year and was six feet long, so I was in good shape.)

Now, I couldn't get it to connect right away. The short troubleshooter on the insert says to reboot your modem, then to reboot the router. I did. Several times. The computer refused to acknowledge the new router! I was ready to just reconnect my Linksys when I decided to go against all logic and swap the ethernet and modem cords. For many years, computers and peripherals have been fairly color-coded to make it easier for non-tekkies to hook things up. In this case for the TP Link, the ethernet ports (there are four) are yellow and the modem port is blue. I even had previously bought color-coded wires so I didn't accidentally pull the wrong one. After 45 minutes of not being able to connect, I take another look at the back. Everything is in the right spot. But, since I wasn't connecting anyway, I decided to swap out the modem cord and ethernet cord, plugging yellow into the blue slot and the blue cord into the yellow slot. Totally backwards. As you might guess, it took off immediately! So apparently, our unit was either labeled backwards or connected backwards on the inside. Seriously strange. But as long as it works, I don't much care.

The default setting of this router is PUBLIC, so be sure to change your settings to PRIVATE NETWORK, if you don't want everyone in the neighborhood to try and tap into your network. Yes, they would need your password, but there are a lot of smart hackers out there, so you just never know. Better safe than sorry. There are default settings for the account name, network name (your SSID) and passwords, so you will need to change those as soon as you can. (If you forget to write them down, there is a reset button on the back to rol it back to the default passwords.) I also had to change the other settings to WPA2 for our area for the home network. No big deal, just different from before.

The TP Link C9 runs two parallel bands - 2.4Ghz, which is what most home routers use for regular internet access and browsing, and a 5.0 Ghz band, which is for streaming videos and movies. The nice thing about this router, is that if you name BOTH the 2.4 and the 5.0 the same name, it will AUTOMATICALLY switches to the strongest network for your use. I love that! The on/off switch is on the back of the router, so it won't easily get bumped. While my photos show the antennas straight up (we haven't had to move any of them to get a better reception), they rotate and bend towards whatever area you might need a little boost.

Has our reception improved? Yes! The downstairs computer now cruises like it was directly connected to a wired access point. The kids can watch movies and I can browse the net without anyone slowing down. The reception range is fabulous - we live in a multi-unit building, and could probably provide internet connection to all four units. It offers connection speeds of 1.3Gbps over the clearer 5GHz bandwidth and 600Mbps on the 2.4GHz bandwidth. We have not yet found a dead spot in our place - even outside picks up the signal.

In addition to the fabulous signal and great connection speeds, this router can also handle your USB 2.0 and 3.0 devices. There are ports on the side of the router, so you can easily transfer files, photos or data from an external drive to your own computer, or even hook up your printer to print wirelessly. (I haven't tried that yet, but the possibilities are there.)

It also offers a "tether" function for your smartphones. I have not used that, and won't be using that, but it would be great for parents who want to monitor network access/usage from work for their older kids. It is nice to know that option is there.

I am so very pleased with this router! I probably would not have looked at this brand, since I tend to stick with the equipment companies I've had previous success with, but I cannot state enough that this would be an asset to anyone's home network setup.
text_fidelity_b: TP-Link AC1900 Smart Wireless Router - Beamforming Dual Band Gigabit WiFi Internet Routers for Home, High Speed, Long Range, Ideal for Gaming (Archer C9)

text_fidelity_a:
TP-Link AC750 Wireless Wi-Fi Gigabit Router (Archer C2) I am not super "techie" like some of the other folks reviewing this router, just your average housewife who likes gadgets and tries not to drown in the constant wave of weekly tech improvements. As such, I wanted a new router to replace our two year old dual band Belkin with similar speed output, but only a single antenna. The Belkin had a number of dead spots despite using one of those extender things and I had had enough. Enter this TP-Link router.

I was wary of the installation after seeing some other reviews and the difficulties folks have been reporting. However, after reading the box and the instructions fully FIRST and then following the directions exactly, I had no problems. One thing I did notice immediately, is this router is meant to be used with a cable modem and that modem must be powered off before you connect it to this router. I used the website installation method and was up and going in a total of 20 minutes - that is from opening the box to having all our wireless stuff connected to the internet again. The website management page is very detailed and allows for a lot of customization of your network, honestly, more than I need or understand. But changing the router's password and setting our network name was simple and worked on the first try.

After three days of use I like it. The speed is decent and the dual antenna set up has improved the coverage problem we were having with the old Belkin router. I haven't experienced any slowdown or degradation of connectivity with multiple devices going at once thus far. A Fire Phone surfing the net, Fire tablet streaming music, laptop doing email, and a smart tv streaming video all at once in different rooms. So...a good router for every day family use in a pretty typical home.

*********** UPDATE FEBRUARY 2015 ***********
After 90 days this router is trouble free and really working like a champ. Our cable company upgraded our modem and increased our internet speeds recently, requiring a full shutdown and reconnect of my entire network. It was a snap and the router has had no problem with faster connection and the new modem. I relocated everything to the center of our house when everything was being swapped out and the router is now sending a five bar signal out to the back deck, which means I can sit out there with the dogs in nice weather to do email etc.

*****************UPDATE APRIL 2016 *************

I'm still using this router every single day for literally every single WiFi device in our house and it just does its job with zero drama every day. We now have two tablets, two smartphones, three DVR boxes on WiFi, two laptops, a printer, a Fire Stick for streaming movies, a smart tv connected the web now and then, and the Echo that's connected all the time. (yeah, I know...we watch a LOT of television in this house!)

Right this minute I am streaming music on the Echo, recording tv shows on two different DVR boxes, using my laptop to update this review, and uploading 42 photos from my phone to the cloud and pushing email to my tablet. Oh - and I am sitting outside on the patio enjoying the lovely spring day. This router is powerful and I have no dead spots inside or out in the backyard.
text_fidelity_b: TP-Link AC750 Wireless Wi-Fi Gigabit Router (Archer C2)

text_fidelity_a:
NETGEAR RangeMax Wireless Router (WNR1000-100NAS (G54/N150)) UPDATE: Six months in, this router has been flawless. AND I've discovered it has its own dynamic DNS support capability. That's a nice feature if you run any sort of server application. So, I continue to be impressed with this product.

---

I will be keeping a close eye on this router, which I just purchased yesterday, because it seems too good to be true. So far, in my 24 hours of usage since purchasing it for $29 at Walmart (sorry, Amazon, I was in a hurry) I have found it to be flexible and powerful in my unusual application, which is remote and requires 100% uptime with occasional bursts of heavy usage. Mine is a factory-fresh rather than refurb unit, incidentally.

I'll admit I had some trouble believing a router this cheap could be as good as this one turned out to be (assuming it stays reliable-- but, the one I bought trumpets a lifetime guarantee on the box). I expected something dumbed-down, with seriously constrained functionality and annoying firmware. (This model's v3 hardware, although Broadcom BCM5356-based, is not compatible with alternative firmware such as DD-WRT due to its problematic NVRAM size.) It's a single-stream design, with an internalized antenna, potentially suggesting performance limitations. And it's from Netgear, which I've frankly not had great luck with before... but it's been years since I've tried one of their products, and the reviews here are generally good. Most of the negative reviews here relate to support experiences, but my networking knowledge-level is expert, so ...what the heck, did I mention it was $29? An easy roll of the dice.

Though my application requires custom configuration, I initially started the unit using its web-based wizard, which you access by connecting your computer (via cable or WiFi) and pointing your browser to 192.168.1.1. With the unit connected to my cable modem, it set itself up quickly and voila, Internet. For most people this would be good enough and the job would be done. Kudos to Netgear for delivering the product with WPA-2 encryption enabled! They provide a SSID and password on a printed label. So, you're good to go. And its default configuration is just fine for most folks' usage.

For my application, however, I needed to cable several devices including a VoIP adaptor (a la [...] and a server with several ports exposed to the Internet. The unit needed to be set to a specific IP address scheme, SSID and password. And a dynamic-DNS utility on the server needed to communicate with my DNS provider. ...To accomplish these and other advanced tasks, the browser-based configurator at 192.168.1.1 has an Advanced tab. Proceeding through the settings is straightforward and similar to other reasonably-configurable routers. The default settings established earlier by the wizard remain intact in the Advanced panes so you are starting from a known-operable configuration. All good.

So I proceeded through each of my customizations, taking care to click the Apply button after modifying any pane. Usually there's a ten-second delay during which the unit sets up the new settings; a few necessitate that the router reboot itself. Everything went smoothly.

So, for $29 I'd replicated an unusual configuration and everything was working. But how well?

Okay so my wife had to take an important international FaceTime call as I was finishing up. So, for a while there the server was downloading some massive updates, two ssh clients were talking to the server, VoIP was in use, six WiFi clients were doing whatever they were doing, a 3G microcell tower was initializing and downloading firmware updates to itself ...and FaceTime was running smoothly with a high frame-rate on her third-gen iPad. A nice acid test!

In particular, I did not feel the need to mess with the unit's default QoS settings... and additional props to Netgear for including QoS in a router this inexpensive!

So far, I'm impressed. It's hard to imagine a better value in a router. I'll update this review if there are any reliability issues, but so far, so good. So excellent, in fact.
text_fidelity_b: NETGEAR RangeMax Wireless Router (WNR1000-100NAS (G54/N150))

CTVISION 4K 8MP Home Business Wired Security Camera Systems,8-Channel 4K 8MP PoE Network Video Recorder(4TB HDD),8pc 4K (4X1080P) Outdoor Dome PoE IP Camera,Free App,P2P Cloud,Onvif,Video Surveillance [[VIDEOID:5b880a1d8f11ab783ee7340a330164be]] I ordered the ‘CTVISION 4K 8MP Home Business Wired Security Camera Systems,8-Channel 4K 8MP PoE Network Video Recorder(4TB HDD),8pc 4K (4X1080P) Outdoor Dome PoE IP Camera,Free App,P2P Cloud,Onvif,Video Surveillance’ for review and would like to share my thoughts.

I will lay this out as pros and cons and give some final thoughts.

Pros: The kit as a whole is well made.
Cameras are well made.
The 4tb hard drive is a good name brand and seems to be performing quite well.
The video quality is good.
The kit comes with 8X good quality 50 foot CAT5 cables (more on this in the cons)

Cons: The included cables are only 50 feet each. In a home install, if you are trying to run cameras to all corners of your house, 50 feet is not long enough in my case. I only used three of these cables. I had to buy more cable (CAT6) for the longer runs.
Although the cameras are well made, because they are of the Dome type, if you adjust the cameras to point at much of an angle, you run into issues at night when the IR lights turn on. This causes the IR lights to reflect back at the cameras (See attached video) The best angle for the cameras are to point straight down or at a very slight angle.
Speaking of angles, these cameras only have a 90 degree diagonal viewing angle which was a little disappointing.
When viewing the live feed, sometimes the video feed gets distorted for a couple of seconds.
The software of the NVR is a little overwhelming and hard to navigate. This is probably due to the fact that I have never used this type of system before. There are a lot of options in the Software which does not work with these specific cameras, such as Human Detection or PTZ (Pan Tilt Zoom). Not having the PTZ is really no big deal but it would have been nice to have the Human Detection so that the cameras don’t alarm when the wind blows the trees and shrubs.
There is an option to send an email when there is motion detected on the cameras but I was never able to get that to work.
Although there is an email option, I would have liked to see a text option.

Overall I am actually happy with this kit. It at least provides peace-of-mind knowing that the cameras are always recording and with the included 4tb hard drive in this kit, it provides many hours of footage. I hope that this was somewhat helpful.
text_fidelity_b: CTVISION 4K 8MP Home Business Wired Security Camera Systems,8-Channel 4K 8MP PoE Network Video Recorder(4TB HDD),8pc 4K (4X1080P) Outdoor Dome PoE IP Camera,Free App,P2P Cloud,Onvif,Video Surveillance

Geeni Sentry Wi-Fi Wireless Smart Floodlight Security Camera, 2-Way Audio, Motion Sensor Alarm, Audio Video Recording, Works with Alexa and Hey Google I have had the opportunity to review a few similar products over the last couple years and this new security light by Sentry has some great features that make it a stand out among other security lights.

I found installation straightforward and simple. For those who have trouble connecting to your WiFi, the most common issue is the strength of the different frequencies your router is broadcasting. The easiest way to resolve this is to go into your router settings via your computer and turn off the 5 GHz band during setup. This is necessary sometimes when initially setting up SmartHome products. While some may find this necessary for this product, I did not using my Orbi router system.

The Geeni App is easy to use and makes setup and customization of how the light operates user friendly.

This unit puts out a huge amount of light - 2100 Lumens to be exact while only using 24 watts of power thanks to it utilizing the LED bulbs.

This is the first security bulb I have reviewed that actually has a built in siren. This could be an outstanding feature if needed. Whether utilized to scare off someone attempting to break in to your home or to cause unwanted pests to run the other way - it will work! This siren is effective because it’s loud.

The speaker can also be used for communication purposes. By utilizing a built in microphone you’ll be able to have conversations with those you are viewing through the camera. The speaker and microphone have a surprisingly high clarity. The only thing I found odd with this aspect of this product is this is not a light you’ll want to place at head height as the light is so bright and the camera is really made to provide a wide angle view. Therefore when you speak through the speaker I found people usually look around and can’t figure out the source of the disembodied voice.

After using this product for the last 6 weeks I have found that it performs excellently. By installing a 128GB micro SD card within it, saving videos is easy and I’ve had plenty of time to review the footage. I love that it holds the recording locally so there is no cloud subscription fee required.

This is an excellent security light that will not only light the night when motion is detected, but will record it, alert you, scare the intruder with a siren or allow you to speak to them (or apologize for just scaring them with the siren).

This is an outstanding product that I definitely recommend.
text_fidelity_b: Geeni Sentry Wi-Fi Wireless Smart Floodlight Security Camera, 2-Way Audio, Motion Sensor Alarm, Audio Video Recording, Works with Alexa and Hey Google

Logitech Wireless Headset for iPad, iPhone and iPod Touch The positives about these headphones outnumber the negatives.

In no particular order;

1. Easy set up. Like all bluetooth devices, these headphones were a quick set up by simply turning them on and my mac responded with 'Do You Want To Use This Device?' The total set up time, approximately sixty seconds!

2.Excellent for VOIP gmail phone.

3. You can charge the headset, while you are using it. So on marathon conference call days, I can plug them in, while using them for about twenty minutes and then they are charged enough to last through a long, boring, three hour conference call (more's the pity!).

4. They charge off the USB port and they come with a cable for doing this.

5. They are lightweight and comfortable to wear, so no headaches!

6. Adjustable volume which is perfect for the hard of hearing.

The negatives, in no particular order;

1. The sound quality is not so great. It is too grainy for music, there is a static sound in the background of everything you are listening to, not a big deal if you are using them for phone conversations, but a definite loser if you are trying to listen to music.

text_fidelity_a:
VANGUARD GH-200 Tripod Heads This is my 2nd GH-200 tripod head. The first one I received through the Vine program was defective and was returned to Vanguard and exchanged. The replacement I received operates much better than the first.

I tested this tripod head with my [[ASIN:B001D60LG8 Dolica AX620B100 62-Inch Proline Tripod]] and my Kodak Z990 camera.

At full tension release there is just enough friction to give some confident feedback of movement. It allows responsive and fairly easy tracking of moving objects. The tension knob has approximately ¼ turn of adjustment giving some range of friction preferences. At full lock I found the head to be rock solid with no play or give. The pistol grip has a release handle that allows you to set the tension knob to full lock but have the ability to squeeze the grip and quickly reposition the camera. The spring in the grip is not adjustable and is insanely stiff. After a half hour of testing out this tripod head my hand was aching from the force necessary to squeeze the grip release. In their product description they claim you can track an object "ultra smoothly by pressing the trigger" I did not find this to be the case. You can reposition the camera by squeezing the trigger but at full lock the grip release did not give smooth movement or ease of tracking.

The pistol grip has a quick, one hand operation, release collar that allows the grip to be rotated 360 degrees with eight locking points. This collar and release are affected by the friction setting for the ball head.

I'm not a fan of their mounting system. First because the screw to attach the plate to the camera does not have a butterfly handle. A coin or screwdriver is required to mount or dismount the plate from or to the camera. Second, while partially released the plate can be adjusted forward or back to get better balance of your rig. There is a pin on the head keeping the plate and camera from falling forward or backward off the mount. Unfortunately there is no positive safety lock. Just a few turns on the tension knob for the camera plate and your camera is completely free of the head.

The mounting plate itself can be unlocked to turn 360 degree panoramic shots. There are 72 click points that are 5 degrees of rotation apart. Even with my relatively light Kodak Z990 on this head the clicks became indistinct and hard to notice. Still, it's a nice feature to capture smooth panoramic shots.

The tripod mount is threaded for 1/4" or, with an easily removed adapter sleeve, 3/8" screw. This tripod head did not come with the small tool to remove the adapter sleeve that other Vanguard products do but as with the camera plate a screwdriver or coin will do the job.

In the end I can't say I'm a complete fan of this tripod head. Itappears to be quite sturdy and should give years of service. Unfortunately, for me, the lack of secure locking of the camera plate and the extreme pressure needed to squeeze the trigger release we enough negatives to make this less than stellar. I can't say that I was wow'd by it.
text_fidelity_b: VANGUARD GH-200 Tripod Heads

FiiO X5 High Resolution Music Player (2nd Generation)(Titanium) I have used this DAP for about two years now, and I am very pleased with it. It sounds terrific, and I absolutely love the built-in Line-out function for getting the best possible audio into my other devices.
The interface is a little strange and old-fashioned if you’re used to an iPhone. It’s like a weird iPod, but it’s worse. The scroll wheel doesn’t feel nearly as good as the iPod’s, but it’s still a great way to get around in the interface. The interface responds quickly, and has never glitched or frozen on me.
For music navigation, I always use the folder browsing, to browse through the memory cards using my own organization. This is because of two big failures in the built-in browsing:
1. When browsing by genre, you simply get a listing of EVERY track in that Genre alphabetically. So if I select “Classical”, the next screen simply shows me page after page of tracks that start with “1”.
2. When browsing by artist, it uses the actual “Artist” field, instead of “Album Artist”. That’s a little old fashioned now, and most devices are smart enough to use the album artist. It makes it impossible to browse for an album where there are multiple guest artists, but the album itself should all be under one artist.
To do my organization, I have found that JRiver Media Center. That does NOT come with this - you are on your own for software.
I decided on the X5 after looking into the DAC chips Fiio used, and verifying that this could play the formats I was interested - specifically DSD and 24 bit 192KHz PCM. It does both of those with no trouble, and sounds great doing it. Most of my music is in high-resolution FLAC, and CD-resolution Apple Lossless. They both play very well on the X5.
Most of the time, I use mine with a Fiio E12A Mont Blanc Special Edition headphone amp, and Shure SE215 In-Ear monitors. I will also sometimes connect it using the line-out port to my car AUX input or my home stereo. It sounds great in all cases.
I have used it a few times as an external DAC for my Mac, and it works really well at that too - that allows me to connect my headphones through the amp and get some terrific sound.
It has no moving parts, and I can’t imagine that anything on it will break for a very long time thanks to the sturdy aluminum case. If it ever does, I think the only change I would want in my next DAC would be USB-C (the Micro USB connector is just so flimsy on ALL devices, not just this). I don’t need a bigger screen, and I certainly don’t need any more quality.
text_fidelity_b: FiiO X5 High Resolution Music Player (2nd Generation)(Titanium)

text_fidelity_a:
Lexar JumpDrive S47 128GB USB 3.1 Flash Drive (LJDS47-128ABBKNA) I have had a need for an additional storage solution for my laptop which will enable me to back up files, and transfer between desktop (my workstation) and my laptop when necessary. My goal is to have it as an alternative mini hard drive, so to speak. Let's take a Look.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This is a tiny Jumpdrive, for those who have never used one, it is similar in appearance to a dongle that you use for wireless keyboard or mouse in the USB port. It does not have a case and the packaging is rather difficult to open.

WHAT IS THIS FOR?
This is designed not to carry with you all of the time like some of the flash drives, but to use almost as a mini hard drive and keep it in your laptop or even desktop if desired. It will keep your files handy, has a pretty fast transfer rate, and has a decent amount of storage, depending on what kind of files you plan to store on it.

WHAT ELSE CAN YOU USE THESE FOR?
This can also be theoretically used to keep in the car as a way to play music on your sound system via USB port. I have not been able to do that yet as I have had some issues setting up the right format. I am not sure how security will interact with that..

DOES THIS HAVE SECURITY ON IT?
This drive has a program called ENCDataVault Lite. That will allow you to encrypt your files and have them accessed with a password you set up in case you lose your drive at least your files will be somewhat protected unless it is a hacker who finds it.

HOW IS TRANSFER RATE?
I have used this in a USB3.0 as well as USB2.0 port and both worked well.

DOES THIS FIT TYPE C CONNECTION?
You can not use this in a type C port so please check your laptop or desktop prior to purchase to be sure you have an actual USB port to use this in that is not already being used.

WHAT I DON'T LIKE ABOUT THIS
This drive should come with a tiny case on a keychain or with at least a loop handle on it so that you can put it somewhere safe and not lose it. It does not come with that. Something this small needs to have a colorful case to make it harder to lose. I know that the idea is to have it stay in the unit you use it on mostly, but sometimes you have to take it out and it needs a case.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a tiny drive. It is meant to use in either a car sound system (USB port), on a laptop or desktop that you plan to use it on regularly, and not be moved around constantly. It does not come with any kind of case at all to store it in when not in a port. It does have encryption which is a big plus to theoretically protect files in case of loss.

MY RATING
FOUR STARS. The performance is top notch. The fact that this does not come with a case is worth removing a star. Ideally it would not be a problem most of the time, but I still think that it needs protective COLORFUl case for those times you need to remove it from a port and take it from one place to another.
text_fidelity_b: Lexar JumpDrive S47 128GB USB 3.1 Flash Drive (LJDS47-128ABBKNA)

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Performance MX Wireless Mouse (DISCONTINUED and Replaced by MX Master 2S) howdy y'all,

i bought this mouse to replace my logitech mx1100 cordless mouse. that one finally had the left mouse button start doing the dreaded false double click. it lasted several years, so i was not seriously annoyed. [*grin*]

for those coming from an mx1100, here are differences i noticed ...
- the mx1100 had the hump in the center instead of towards the back, so the main mouse buttons were shorter
this makes the mouse seem really rather too long. i am unsure if that will bother me once i use the new one for a while.

- the mx1100 had less of a slant to the right so that my hand sat a bit closer to level
the new one is more comfy for my very right-handed self.

- the mx1100 mouse wheel projected a tad more
combined with the sharp slant, the new mouse wheel feels like it is tilted the wrong way. it isn't, but i keep finding my finger on the right edge of the wheel instead of directly on the wheel.

- the mx1100 mouse wheel had a more pronounced side-move feel
the new mouse is very subtle. i liked the distinct feel of the older one when it toggled the side-move "button" function of the mouse wheel. of course, i like clicky keyboards, too ... [*grin*]

- the mx1100 had the upper thumb buttons just below the upper left edge
the new mouse has them on a surface that slants very sharply down to the left from the left edge. it makes the reach to the forward/back buttons a tad less comfy. combine that with a taper on those two buttons and i have found myself looking to see where the darned buttons went. they are also a tad more to the front of the mouse.
these admittedly annoying things that will likely fade out of my attention with use.

- the mx1100 used two AA rechargeable batteries
the new mouse uses one. since i use a lot of battery powered devices, i have a battery charger and several spares on hand. that means i will likely not use the usb charging function very often. still, one AA is better than having to charge two! [*grin*]

- the mx1100 had a larger usb wireless adapter
the new one is quite tiny! it works well - i put it on the back of my system among the tangle of wires that connect to other things and have had no reception problems.

*****
the parts list says there otta be a driver cd included. _not_ so! [*sigh ...*] you are referred to their download site if you want to use any of the extended functions or buttons. the performance mx has a $100 recommended price and there is no excuse to cheap out like that. thankfully, win7x32 has basic mouse support for the standard buttons, the mouse wheel, and the back/forward buttons.

this is a /_serious_/ fubar and i almost subtracted a star from my rating because of it.
*****

i suspect that folks with short hands will have problems with this mouse, but i am getting used to it already. i'm 6'1" and my hand is 7.5" from base to middle finger tip. not a _large_ hand, but not short.

*****
rated a THREE since it does what i expected - no more and no less. still, i came very close to rating this a two for not including the cd.

take care,
lee
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Performance MX Wireless Mouse (DISCONTINUED and Replaced by MX Master 2S)

While it does most of what they advertise the BT connectivity is really poor unless you hold the phone in a stationary visible position from your phone or while it's stationary on a table. If you put it in your pocket or even in your hand with a normal hand swing the sound stutters and is not worth using. I've purchased a 60 dollar pair of similar BT ear buds without all the extra features but it sure does work reliably in a way you would expect any headset to work. I've written their technical support for assistance and this is what they told me after a few emails back and forth explaining my issue and running their tests. Here is their final reply, I didn't put in the agents name as to not hold the agent responsible directly for this issue.

(Bragi)
Apr 5, 10:26 CEST
Hello Derek

Thanks for getting back to us with the results of your test.

I understand The Black Dash has some issues when being connected to an external device via Bluetooth, specifically when using it outside. In certain cases we have had a few customers who experienced similar issues like you. As you performed the range test and got a positive result, we can confidently say that your unit's Bluetooth hardware is generally working correctly.

Nonetheless, this is not an excuse for your Bluetooth dropouts. Bluetooth, in general is a technology that offers us the possibility to pair The Black Dash to many different devices, due to the technology's widespread usage. Never the less, it is also a technology that comes with disadvantages. One of those is the actual dependency of the surroundings as you discovered already. That actually means that Bluetooth works very well in closed surroundings where you have surfaces that reflect the Bluetooth signals. However, when being outside with no walls at all, the Bluetooth range very much varies. Having your external device in your right side pockets, your The Black Dash should work independently from the outside surroundings.

Again, this is not an excuse for your Bluetooth dropouts, but rather an explanation for this behavior. Furthermore, we are doing our best to regulate Bluetooth performance with our firmware settings, and every update should actually improve Bluetooth performance.
We hope you can understand that.

All the best,
(Agent name)& your Team Bragi​​​​​​

Transcend 16 GB Class 6 SDHC Flash Memory Card TS16GSDHC6 I have been using Panasonic SDHC Class 6 4GB cards, and have been pretty happy with them. I decided to get this one just because of the low price and high ratings, and am pleased to find that I agree with the many 5-star reviews.

Some information I didn't see in the other reviews, in case it's of interest: I ran a write test with a big file on my computer, and saw write speeds consistently above 6MB/s, as you ought to expect for a Class 6. (Among other things, that means of course that your camera can get ready for the next shot just that much faster because it's spending less time waiting for the recording to be completed.)

I didn't bother with a read test, since read speed is rarely an issue.

A comment on SD card readers/writers. As many have said, older SD devices, including older cameras, will not work with SDHC cards. My old card adapter (Sandisk 8-in-1) hung when I put this chip in. But my newer adapters (a built-in slot, and an Edge All-in-1) worked just fine. So if you're having trouble, this is possibly the first thing to check.
text_fidelity_b: Transcend 16 GB Class 6 SDHC Flash Memory Card TS16GSDHC6

text_fidelity_a:
Belkin Verve Folio Case with Stand for Samsung Galaxy Tab 10.1inch (Black) After purchasing my tablet, I had found a case for it at Walmart, very sturdy, adequately padded, and with the ability to tilt the screen. However, the mechanism to tilt the screen was established with velcro, which after a while did not hold as well as it did in the beginning. In addition, at least one of the little elastic straps that held the tablet in the case pressed on the power button, sometimes with bizarre results. I therefore considered this Belkin case with interest.

Upon receiving, I immediately fitted the tablet into the case, and was delighted when it was held snugly and kept from slipping out by a flap which tucks under the tablet. All the buttons except the charging button were close to a cutout so that button could be accessed easily. In addition, the cover of the case has little grooves at intervals so that the tablet can be propped up to be viewed at various angles.

As other reviewers have mentioned, it's a very sturdy and thick case, which does increase the weight of the featherlight Galaxy Tab somewhat. And as I have been careful not to drop it, I do not know how well it protects and from various heights...and nor am I likely to test! But it appears very solid, and the elastic cord sewn into the case cover keeps it closed well.

Drawbacks: there's no hole for the charger, so you must charge with the case open. Nor can you charge when using the tablet propped up. And you can only prop horizontally, not vertically, although I doubt if that is much of an issue for most of the things you would want to do with the tablet propped up.

In short, it's not perfect because of the case having to be open to charge, and I also wish there was some way to keep my stylus inside; the case is so tight that I have to hang it outside, exposing the tip to dirt and damage. But otherwise it works well for me. Your mileage may vary!
text_fidelity_b: Belkin Verve Folio Case with Stand for Samsung Galaxy Tab 10.1inch (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Microsoft Wireless Rechargeable Laser Mouse 7000 Mac/Windows I have mixed feelings about this mouse. On one hand it is a pleasure to use. On the other, charging it leaves much to be desired.

This is a fairly large mouse, sculpted nicely to fit most peoples' hands. I have large hands and I have found this mouse to be a good fit. It is comfortable to grip, the scroll wheel is smooth and easy to turn, and the buttons are easy to press without being hyper-sensitive. Ergonomics are this mouse's strongest attribute.

In use, the mouse is on par with other Microsoft mice I have used. It is accurate. Unlike some of the comments by other reviewers here, I have had no issue with it being too sensitive or too precise. The performance has, in my opinion, been average. This is not a bad thing - Microsoft mice are usually very consistent and this one fits the norm.

Where I ran into difficulty with this mouse was in charging it. I read a lot of other reviews on this mouse beforehand so I was prepared for issues with charging. That said, I was still having issues getting the mouse to charge the battery until I cut part of a 3x5 index card, folded it up and crammed it into the battery compartment with the battery. There have been enough other people that have had to do similarly odd things to rule out the possibility of this being an isolated case.

The battery can be put into a normal charger, but that defeats the purpose.

This is not a bad mouse. It's actually quite good and I would recommend it except for the recharging issue. As a wireless mouse it is fine, but as a recharging mouse it needs a design revisit.
text_fidelity_b: Microsoft Wireless Rechargeable Laser Mouse 7000 Mac/Windows
